catch_records.source_excerpt: The Dolphin AM trip called in with 60+ Barracuda, 30+ Bonito up to 12lbs, and 2 Yellowtail for 40 anglers so far on their morning trip. They also reported great conditions on the water. There's probably going to be a light load this afternoon so be sure to make reservations.
The Pacific Queen is up to 76 Yellowfin Tuna (mostly 20 to 40 lbs.) 2 Wahoo, and 1 Marlin for 30 anglers on a 2 day trip. Also, they reported beautiful, flat calm weather to start off their day.
The Dolphin called in from a 3/4 day trip with 79 Skip jack tuna up to 10 pounds and 23 Yellowfin tuna up to 15 pounds for 31 anglers
The Tribute returned from their 1.5 Day trip with 22 yellowfin tuna (up to 70#), 30 skipjack, and 10 bonito.
The Tribute returned from their 1.5 Day trip with 22 yellowfin tuna (up to 70#), 30 skipjack, and 10 bonito.

The San Diego on their full day bagged 151 Yellowfin Tuna and 220 Skipjack for their 35 anglers! Recommended setups for the San Diego has been a 20lb-25lb setup along with a 30lb-40lb setup for anchovies and sardines. Small jigs have been seeing decent response for the anglers looking to throw artificials.Passports are Not currently required for this trip.

The Sea Watch finished up their full day trip with 104 Yellowfin Tuna and 44 Skipjack Tuna. Current sniper style jigs have been getting bit well but also good to have a 20-25lb live bait setup. The Sea Watch has spots available for tomorrow and Saturday! Passports are Not currently required for this trip.

The Sea Watch finished up their full day trip with 104 Yellowfin Tuna and 44 Skipjack Tuna. Current sniper style jigs have been getting bit well but also good to have a 20-25lb live bait setup. The Sea Watch has spots available for tomorrow and Saturday! Passports are Not currently required for this trip.

The New Seaforth on this morning's 1/2 day landed 4 Yellowfin, 2 Bonito, 5 Bullet tuna and 18 Skipjack! The New Seaforth has plenty of room on tomorrow's PM trip! Make those reservations or come on down. A 20-25lb setup would be recommended for these fish along with hooks from #4-2/0. Rod rentals and fishing licenses are available at the landing during check-in.

southern_california.text: The marine pattern is fairly steady through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 4-12 kt; morning is favored on 6 of 7 days. Combined seas range 2.0-4.0 ft with 7-18 sec periods. Best current windows: 10-31 PM, 11-05 AM, 11-06 AM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

Combined seas range 3.0-7.0 ft with 8-16 sec periods. Best current windows: 10-31 AM, 11-02 PM, 11-04 PM. Safety screen blocks: 11-01. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The anglers were fishing for rock fish and sea bass today. There were some sea bass caught near South Rock and Natural Bridges. The rock fishing was good at South Rock and Davenport. The few anglers looking for bluefin said it was a little bumpy. I did not get many tuna reports except bonito. The swell was a little bigger and the wind came up in the afternoon on the near shore waters.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast October 22, 2026 Bluefin Tuna Give North Coast Anglers a Reason for Optimism Bluefin tuna are making a late-season appearance off the North Coast. Jake Mitchell of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing and fellow anglers from Shelter Cove have landed bluefin weighing 30 to 60 pounds, with most of the action occurring 10 to 30 miles offshore. Photo courtesy of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing. After hearing reports of bluefin tuna being caught out of Fort Bragg, Jake Mitchell of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing and a few other boats from Shelter Cove decided it was worth taking a look. Last Thursday, as they headed southwest from the Cove, they came across a couple of schools of bluefin. “We were lucky to get one fish that day,” said Mitchell. “Since then, there have been 11 more bluefin landed, with Monday being the most productive day.” The fleet grew by Wednesday, but the fishing had slowed. “I don’t think there’s a big concentration of fish out there, but that could change,” Mitchell said. “Most of the fish have been caught between 10 and 30 miles offshore. They haven’t been huge, but most are running between 30 and 60 pounds. Trolling Madmacs and spreader bars has worked for us.” Conditions

field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: The ocean weather not all that good right now but we are expecting pretty good ocean weather for fishing this Friday coming up thru the weekend. The Surfrider and the Tacklebuster will be running our fishing trips this weekend.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
